components.css: .ds-band { position: relative; overflow: hidden; padding: 32px; border-radius: 24px; color: #fff; font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; background: radial-gradient(closest-side at 85% 110%, rgba(255,255,255,0.28), transparent 60%), linear-gradient(160deg, #2f4fe0 0%, #2f4fe0 42%, #7f9cff 100%); box-shadow: 0 30px 60px -32px rgba(33,55,157,0.65); } .ds-band::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0.32; mix-blend-mode: overlay; pointer-events: none; background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='220' height='220'><filter id='n'><feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.75' numOctaves='3' stitchTiles='stitch'/><feColorMatrix type='saturate' values='0'/></filter><rect width='100%' height='100%' filter='url(%23n)'/></svg>"); } .ds-band > * { position: relative; } .ds-band h1 { margin: 0; font-size: 34px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.025em; line-height: 1.25; } .ds-band p { margin: 10px 0 0; max-width: 66ch; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.375; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.84); } .ds-flag { display: inline-flex; margin-top: 16px; padding: 2px 10px; border: 1px dashed rgba(255,255,255,0.6); border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.css: .ds-nodes { display: flex; gap: 24px; padding: 24px; background: #d9e2fd; font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-node { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; gap: 10px; width: 190px; height: 104px; padding: 14px; border-radius: 16px; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 300ms, box-shadow 300ms, border-color 300ms; } .ds-node:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-node:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2f4fe0; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-node b { font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #2443c9; } .ds-node span { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: #0e1a46; } .ds-node i { display: block; height: 4px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #e6ecff; overflow: hidden; } .ds-node em { display: block; height: 100%; background: #4f6ef0; } .ds-done { border: 1px solid transparent; background: linear-gradient(150deg, #2f4fe0 0%, #5a74f2 100%); } .ds-done b { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.8); } .ds-done span { color: #fff; } .ds-done i { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.3); } .ds-done em { background: #fff; } .ds-doing { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.8); backdrop-filter: blur(14px); border: 1px solid #4f6ef0; transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 24px 44px -20px rgba(31,52,160,0.75), 0 0 0 2px #d9e2fd, 0 0 0 4px #2f4fe0; } .ds-todo { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.58); border: 1px dashed #a9bcff; }

narrative.overview:
Isoline is a working table seen through frosted glass: a soft, grain-washed blue ground, translucent bento tiles floating above it, and one saturated cobalt band per page that states the result in a sentence. Everything is a depth of blue. Navy, cobalt, periwinkle and ice carry the hierarchy; the tool families keep their identity as different depths of the same blue (reporting navy, carbon cobalt, environment sky, people indigo), so the product reads as one instrument rather than a set of coloured apps.

The density is that of a consultant's analysis desk: 15px body, compact controls, charts that are presentation-grade the moment they render. Numbers are the heroes and are set large and light (Geist 300, tabular, tight tracking), never bold. Trust is built by provenance rather than decoration: every data tile ends in a ruled source-note collar, and data status is drawn as line form (solid verified, dashed estimated, dotted review) in marks, chart strokes, journey nodes and flags alike.

The category default (white rounded cards with an emerald accent and leaf icons) and the plain grey dashboard are the confirmed rejections. Green exists in the system only as the `ok` state colour.
keyCharacteristics: Frosted glass tiles (58% white, 14px blur, 1.4 saturate, white hairline, blue-tinted shadow, 18px radius) on a grain-washed radial blue ground.
One cobalt-to-periwinkle grain band per page, carrying title, one-sentence result and actions.
Families as depths of blue, scoped by `data-family`; state colours (warn, crit, ok) for meaning only.
Large light tabular numerals in Geist; uppercase tracked labels only for functional metadata.
Source-note collar on every data tile; solid/dashed/dotted line language for data status.
A full dark theme that inverts the ramp to midnight glass, following the OS unless `data-theme` pins it.

rules.name: The Depths-of-Blue Rule
rules.body: Every family, series and structural accent is drawn from the blue hierarchy (navy through ice, plus sky and indigo for two families). A new tool gets a depth of blue, not a new hue.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Amber, red and green appear only when they state review, error/deadline or a positive result. They are never decoration, never a family colour, never a brand accent.

rules.name: The Light Numeral Rule
rules.body: Headline figures are Geist 300 with tabular lining numerals and -0.035em tracking. Weight never stands in for importance on a number; size and the lead tile do.

rules.name: The Tabular Ledger Rule
rules.body: Any number that can be compared (tables, inputs, dates, percentages, chart labels) uses tabular lining numerals.

rules.name: The Blue Shadow Rule
rules.body: In the light theme no shadow is grey or black; every shadow is tinted with deep cobalt (`rgba(31,52,160,…)` or `rgba(33,55,157,…)`).

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: Grain lives on two surfaces only: the page ground (14% opacity) and the result band (32%, overlay blend). Tiles stay clean so charts remain legible.

dos: Do open every page with exactly one result band that states the outcome in one sentence, with on-band button variants for its actions.
Do end every chart, table and data tile with the source-note collar, including its status line.
Do draw data status as line form everywhere: solid verified, dashed estimated/default, dotted review.
Do set a `data-family` on any tool surface and take accents from `--fam*`, so the family's depth of blue follows automatically.
Do set governing figures in Geist 300 tabular with -0.035em tracking, and lead each figure row with the family-gradient tile.
Do tint every light-theme shadow with deep cobalt and keep tiles on the 58% glass recipe.
Do honour reduced motion: rule-draw, flow march, spin, rise and particles all stop, and transitions drop to 0ms.
donts: Don't introduce a hue outside the blue hierarchy for a family, series or accent; green, amber and red are state colours only.
Don't fall back to the category default of white rounded cards with an emerald accent and leaf icons, or to a plain grey dashboard.
Don't put grain on tiles or charts; it belongs to the ground and the band.
Don't bold a headline figure or use a grey or black drop shadow in the light theme.
Don't use uppercase tracked labels as decorative kickers above headings; they are reserved for functional metadata (group legends, note keys, table headers).
